drowning_deaths.short_description: Annual count of unintentional drowning deaths.
drowning_deaths.long_description: Annual count of deaths from unintentional drowning (ICD-10 underlying cause of death codes W65, W66, W67, W68, W69, W70, W73, W74), from CDC WONDER's Underlying Cause of Death database. Cells representing fewer than 10 deaths are suppressed by CDC; these are filled in here with 5, the midpoint of the suppressed 1-9 range, and marked with suppressed_flag = 1: treat those values as an estimate, not an observed count. A true zero is reported as 0 (suppressed_flag = 0).
drowning_deaths.statement: In {location}, there were {value} unintentional drowning deaths in {time}.

drowning_population.long_name: Population denominator used for the drowning crude rate
drowning_population.short_description: Population denominator for the drowning crude rate.
drowning_population.long_description: Bridged-race population estimate used by CDC WONDER as the denominator for the drowning crude rate, for the matching geography, year, and demographic group. CDC does not publish a denominator for every geography/demographic combination (notably county by age group, where it reports 'Not Applicable'); those cells are coded here as -999 with missing_denom_flag = 1.
drowning_population.statement: In {location}, the population denominator was {value} in {time}.

drowning_crude_rate.long_name: Unintentional drowning death rate per 100,000 population
drowning_crude_rate.short_description: Annual unintentional drowning death rate per 100,000 population.
drowning_crude_rate.long_description: Crude rate of unintentional drowning deaths per 100,000 population, as reported by CDC WONDER's Underlying Cause of Death database (ICD-10 codes W65, W66, W67, W68, W69, W70, W73, W74). Where the death count was suppressed for confidentiality (suppressed_flag = 1, fewer than 10 deaths) the rate is computed from the filled-in count of 5 divided by the population, so it is an estimate. Coded as -999 only where no population denominator exists for that geography and demographic combination (missing_denom_flag = 1).
drowning_crude_rate.statement: In {location}, the unintentional drowning death rate was {value} per 100,000 population in {time}.

drowning_crude_rate_lcl.long_name: Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for the drowning crude rate
drowning_crude_rate_lcl.short_description: Lower 95% confidence bound for the drowning death rate.
drowning_crude_rate_lcl.long_description: Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for drowning_crude_rate, as reported by CDC WONDER. Coded as -999 wherever no bound is available: either CDC did not publish one (flagged by suppressed_flag = 1 or missing_denom_flag = 1), or this is a derived row CDC never itself reports a CI for -- the county-level ten-year age rows, whose crude rate is derived from a population estimated here rather than reported by CDC (see drowning_population). Do not plot error bars wherever this is -999.
drowning_crude_rate_lcl.statement: In {location}, the lower bound of the 95% CI for the drowning death rate was {value} in {time}.

drowning_crude_rate_ucl.long_name: Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for the drowning crude rate
drowning_crude_rate_ucl.short_description: Upper 95% confidence bound for the drowning death rate.
drowning_crude_rate_ucl.long_description: Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for drowning_crude_rate, as reported by CDC WONDER. Coded as -999 wherever no bound is available: either CDC did not publish one (flagged by suppressed_flag = 1 or missing_denom_flag = 1), or this is a derived row CDC never itself reports a CI for -- the county-level ten-year age rows, whose crude rate is derived from a population estimated here rather than reported by CDC (see drowning_population). Do not plot error bars wherever this is -999.
drowning_crude_rate_ucl.statement: In {location}, the upper bound of the 95% CI for the drowning death rate was {value} in {time}.

suppressed_flag.long_name: Flag: death count suppressed by CDC for confidentiality
suppressed_flag.short_description: 1 if CDC suppressed the death count (1-9 deaths) for this row, 0 otherwise.
suppressed_flag.long_description: 1 where CDC WONDER withheld a cell representing 1-9 deaths, 0 otherwise. drowning_deaths is filled in with 5 (the midpoint of 1-9) and drowning_crude_rate is recomputed from it, so suppressed_flag = 1 marks an estimated value; the confidence bounds stay -999. Rows where several cells are combined (e.g. the Overall row summed from the sexes) are flagged if any cell was suppressed.

missing_denom_flag.short_description: 1 if CDC publishes no population for this row, so no rate can be given, 0 otherwise.
missing_denom_flag.long_description: 1 where CDC WONDER reports population as 'Not Applicable' or 'Not Available' for this geography and group (for example Connecticut counties from 2022, whose legacy counties no longer have population estimates), so the population and rate are coded -999. Independent of suppressed_flag; both can be 1 on the same row.

cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.name: CDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death, 2018-2024 (ICD-10, expanded)
cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.organization: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.description: Mortality data from death certificates filed in the 50 states and the District of Columbia, queried through CDC WONDER's Underlying Cause of Death (ICD-10, expanded) database and restricted to unintentional drowning: ICD-10 codes W65 (bathtub), W66 (swimming pool fall), W67 (in swimming pool), W68 (fall into swimming pool), W69 (natural water), W70 (fall into natural water), W73 (other specified drowning/submersion), and W74 (unspecified drowning/submersion). Data are broken out separately by age group, sex, single race, and Hispanic origin (each queried independently, not cross-tabulated), at both the state and county level, for years 2018-2024. State and county both use CDC WONDER's Ten-Year Age Groups (<1, 1-4, 5-14, 15-24, ..., 85+), but the two levels differ in how population is sourced. At the state level, CDC WONDER reports Population and Crude Rate directly for Ten-Year Age Groups. At the county level, CDC WONDER reports Deaths only for this age variable -- Population and Crude Rate remain checked (mandatory) in the query form but the server omits them from the export regardless, for every state and year. County-level population is therefore derived here by summing CDC's Five-Year Age Groups county population export into the same Ten-Year buckets (e.g. 5-9 + 10-14 = 5-14); crude_rate is then recomputed from that derived population rather than taken from CDC directly, so drowning_crude_rate_lcl/_ucl are not populated for county-level age rows (a valid confidence interval needs CDC's own interval method, which this derivation does not replicate). This also surfaces a further CDC limitation: county-level population is reported as 'Not Applicable' for the <1, 1-4, and 85+ Five-Year groups nationwide, for every county regardless of size -- so missing_denom_flag = 1 for those three Ten-Year buckets at the county level essentially always, and county-level drowning rates (though not death counts) are structurally unavailable for infants/toddlers and the oldest age group. Suppressed death counts (1-9 deaths) are filled in with 5, the midpoint of the range, and the rate is recomputed from that count; suppressed_flag = 1 marks these estimated rows (confidence bounds stay -999), and a true zero is reported as 0. Values that cannot be computed are coded -999. suppressed_flag = 1 where CDC withheld a cell for confidentiality (any cell representing fewer than 10 deaths); this affects the death count and the rates derived from it, never the population. missing_denom_flag = 1 where no population denominator exists for that geography and demographic combination (CDC reports 'Not Applicable' or 'Not Available', or -- for county-level age specifically -- the Five-Year population export used to derive it was itself missing); this affects the population and the rates derived from it, never the death count. The two are not mutually exclusive and are both 1 on rows carrying both markers, which is common at the county level. National rows (geography 00, in data_state.csv.gz) come from separate CDC WONDER national queries (scrape_national.py) with the same breakdowns, not from summing the states: every state cell with fewer than 10 deaths is suppressed, so a sum of state counts undercounts (2024: 4,087 from the state cells vs 4,201 reported nationally). The all-ages Overall rows (age = Overall, sex and race Overall) at the national, state and county level are CDC WONDER's own totals from separate queries, not sums of other rows. Each geography also has an age = 0-24 row, a single WONDER query over ages 0-24 (national and state: Ten-Year groups <1, 1-4, 5-14, 15-24; county: the equivalent Five-Year groups, because CDC omits county population for Ten-Year groups), so a cell is suppressed only if all of 0-24 has 1-9 deaths. The 0-24 row overlaps the ten-year age rows, so do not sum across age.
cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.restrictions: Data Use Restrictions: The Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 242m(d)) provides that the data collected by the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) may be used only for the purpose for which they were obtained; any effort to determine the identity of any reported cases, or to use the information for any purpose other than for health statistical reporting and analysis, is against the law. Therefore users will: (1) Use these data for health statistical reporting and analysis only. (2) Do not present or publish birth counts of 9 or fewer or birth rates based on counts of nine or fewer (in figures, graphs, maps, tables, etc.). (3) Make no attempt to learn the identity of any person or establishment included in these data. (4) Make no disclosure or other use of the identity of any person or establishment discovered inadvertently and advise the NCHS Confidentiality Officer of any such discovery: Confidentiality Officer, National Center for Health Statistics, 3311 Toledo Road, Hyattsville, MD 20782. Telephone 888-642-4159. Email: nchsconfidentiality@cdc.gov. Sanctions for Violating Rules: Researchers who violate the terms of the data use restrictions will lose access to WONDER and their sponsors and institutions will be notified. Researchers who are suspected of violating the rules may be prevented from using WONDER until an investigation can be completed. Deliberately making a false statement in any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the Federal government violates 18 USC 1001 and is punishable by a fine of up to $10,000 or up to 5 years in prison, or both..
